audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows contradicted their own why-text and the packet: row 1 said Skill while its why says he keeps the range advantage, row 4 said Gnar while its why says neither side has an edge, and rows 5 and 6 said Riven while both whys say neither side pulls ahead.
audit.why: The packet chart reads Gnar / Gnar / Riven / Riven / Skill / Skill / Skill, and the mirror flipped exactly those four rows from the other side.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 4, 5, 6 flipped as one atomic group across both layers, ratings set to the inverse of the mirror's (row 1 to 3/10, the three Skill rows to 5/10).

audit.whatIsWrong: The first-item spike and whys[5] both build Immortal Shieldbow, while the entry's own itemisation section says Eclipse then Sterak's Gage.
audit.why: A spike keyed to an item the page does not tell the player to buy gives a timing that never arrives.
audit.corrected: spikes[3] and whys[5] rebuilt around Eclipse's spellblade burst layered on Valor's shield, with the all-in tied to Hop's cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings called GNAR! an AOE stun that 'cancels your combo' (whys[4], spikes[2].text), and wants.foe[2] credited the wall slam to Mega Gnar's E.
audit.why: Riot's text is explicit: GNAR! throws enemies and slows them, and only an enemy that HITS A WALL is stunned and takes bonus damage. Mega Gnar's E (Crunch) is a leap that deals area damage with no stun at all — the cone stun is Mega's W, Wallop. Told that his R is a guaranteed AOE stun, the player fights in the open expecting to be stunned anyway; told the truth, standing away from terrain is a free defence.
audit.corrected: whys[4] and spikes[2] now state that GNAR! stuns only on a wall slam and that Wallop is the cone stun; wants.foe[2] moved the wall slam to GNAR! where it belongs.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's defect is 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere' — the entry named no cooldown for any Gnar ability.
audit.why: Hop is Gnar's only escape and it is 22 seconds at rank 1, the longest cooldown in the lane. That single number is the whole all-in trigger; without it 'catch him in mini form' is untimed advice.
audit.corrected: whys[2] now gives Hop's 22-second rank-1 cooldown as the concrete gate, and whys[5] keys the one-item all-in to the same cooldown.

edits.before: Full Q-W-E online: you catch him mid-last-hit in mini form, W-stun prevents his hop, and your Q chain trades favourably before his boomerang returns.
edits.after: Full Q-W-E online: catch him mid-last-hit in mini form and Ki Burst beats Hop, a 22s cooldown at rank 1 — once it is spent he cannot leave your Q chain.

edits.before: His Level 6 is as dangerous as yours: GNAR! transform plus R AOE stun can cancel your combo mid-cast; neither side has a clean edge without reading the bar.
edits.after: His 6 matches yours: GNAR! only stuns if it slams you into a wall, so fight in the open and neither side gets a clean edge — read the Rage bar.

edits.before: Immortal Shieldbow passive layers on your E shield for a double-absorb window, but his first item sheen-powered autos and boomerang damage also scale — neither side pulls clearly ahead.
edits.after: Eclipse layers spellblade burst onto your Valor shield, but his first item and Mega uptime scale just as hard — neither side pulls clearly ahead on one item, so trade on Hop's cooldown.

edits.before: GNAR! transform is Gnar's biggest threat — his Mega AOE stun can cancel your combo and open a free all-in; track the bar before every engage.
edits.after: GNAR! is Gnar's biggest threat — Mega's Wallop stuns in a cone and GNAR! only stuns on a wall, so fight away from terrain and track the Rage bar.

edits.before: Immortal Shieldbow completion is your stabilizer; your E shield stacked on Shieldbow passive lets you absorb one burst-combo and trade back through it.
edits.after: Eclipse completion is your stabilizer; the spellblade burst plus Valor's shield lets you eat one Mega commit and trade straight back through it.

edits.before: Wall-slam you with Mega-Gnar's E during his R AOE stun for a lethal burst window
edits.after: Throw you into a wall with GNAR! — the slam stuns you and adds bonus damage

notes: Left alone deliberately: the champion-template phrase 'third-Q knockup' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.trading and report[3].t. Riot's own text for Broken Wings says the third hit KNOCKS BACK, and the mirror corrected the same thing from Gnar's side, but two of those four strings carry mojibake em dashes in this brief so I could not fix all four together, and fixing two of four would ship the page contradicting itself. Worth a byte-exact pass. Same reason I did not touch 'late', which still names Immortal Shieldbow's passive after spikes[3] and whys[5] moved to Eclipse. Not asserted: whether Mega Gnar's Wallop or GNAR! can interrupt an already-started Broken Wings chain — the kits do not say, and I would not guess it.
